verses.1:1: These are the names of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt with Jacob; each one went in with his household:
verses.1:4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
verses.1:5: Therefore all the souls of those who came out from the thigh of Jacob were seventy; Joseph, however, was in Egypt.
verses.1:6: When he had died, and all his brothers, and all that kindred,
verses.1:7: the sons of Israel grew and, as though sprouting forth, they multiplied; and strengthened exceedingly, they filled the land.
verses.1:8: Meanwhile a new king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
verses.1:9: And he said to his people, "Look, the people of the sons of Israel are numerous and stronger than we are.
verses.1:10: Come, let us wisely oppress them, so that they may not perhaps multiply and, if war breaks out against us, be added to our enemies and, once we are conquered, go out from the land."
verses.1:11: Therefore he set masters of the labors over them, so that they might afflict them with burdens; and they built cities of tabernacles for Pharaoh, Pithom and Rameses.
verses.1:12: And the more they oppressed them, so much the more they multiplied and grew.
verses.1:13: And the Egyptians hated the sons of Israel and afflicted them, mocking them,
verses.1:14: and they brought their life to bitterness with hard labors of clay and brick, and with all servitude by which they were pressed hard in the labors of the earth.
verses.1:15: Now the king of Egypt spoke to the midwives of the Hebrews, of whom one was called Shiphrah, and the other Puah,
verses.1:16: commanding them, "When you act as midwives to the Hebrew women and the time of birth has come, if it is a male, kill him; if a female, spare her."
verses.1:17: But the midwives feared God and did not do according to the command of the king of Egypt, but preserved the males.
verses.1:18: Having summoned them to himself, the king said, "What is this that you wanted to do, that you spared the boys?"
verses.1:19: They answered, "The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women; for they themselves have the knowledge of midwifery, and before we come to them, they give birth."
verses.1:20: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives; and the people grew and was strengthened exceedingly.
verses.1:21: And because the midwives feared God, He built houses for them.
verses.1:22: Therefore Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, "Whatever is born of the male sex, throw into the river; whatever is female, spare."
verses.2:1: After these things a man went out from the house of Levi and took a wife of his own lineage.
verses.2:2: She conceived and bore a son; and seeing him to be handsome, she hid him for three months.
verses.2:3: And when she could no longer conceal him, she took a basket of rushes and coated it with bitumen and pitch; and she placed the little infant inside and set him out in the sedge of the bank of the river,
verses.2:4: while his sister stood at a distance and observed the outcome of the matter.
verses.2:5: Now the daughter of Pharaoh was going down to bathe in the river, and her girls were walking along the edge of the channel. When she saw the basket in the papyrus bed, she sent one of her maidservants; and when it was brought,
verses.2:6: opening it and perceiving in it a little child wailing, she took pity on him and said, "This is one of the infants of the Hebrews."
verses.2:7: The boy's sister said to her, "Do you want me to go and call a Hebrew woman for you who can nurse the little infant?"
verses.2:8: She answered, "Go." The girl went and called her mother.
verses.2:9: Speaking to her, the daughter of Pharaoh said, "Take this boy and nurse him for me; I will give you your wages." The woman received and nursed the boy, and when he was grown, she handed him over to the daughter of Pharaoh.
verses.2:10: She adopted him in the place of a son and called his name Moses, saying, "Because I took him from the water."
verses.2:11: In those days, after Moses had grown up, he went out to his brothers and saw their affliction, and an Egyptian man striking one of his Hebrew brothers.
verses.2:12: And when he had looked around this way and that, and saw that no one was present, he struck the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.
verses.2:13: And going out on the next day, he caught sight of two Hebrews fighting; and he said to the one who was doing the wrong, "Why are you striking your neighbor?"
verses.2:14: He answered, "Who appointed you prince and judge over us? Do you want to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?" Moses was afraid and said, "How has this matter become publicly known?"
verses.2:15: And Pharaoh heard this report and sought to kill Moses; but fleeing from his presence, he stayed in the land of Midian and sat beside a well.
verses.2:16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, who came to draw water; and having filled the troughs, they wanted to water their father's flocks.
verses.2:17: Shepherds came upon them and drove them away; and Moses stood up and, having defended the girls, watered their sheep.
verses.2:18: When they returned to Reuel their father, he said to them, "Why have you come more quickly than usual?"
verses.2:19: They answered, "An Egyptian man delivered us from the hand of the shepherds; moreover, he also drew water with us and gave drink to the sheep."
verses.2:20: But he said, "Where is he? Why did you let the man go? Call him so that he may eat bread."
verses.2:21: Therefore Moses swore that he would live with him. And he took Zipporah his daughter as a wife,
verses.2:22: who bore him a son, whom he called Gershom, saying, "I have been a stranger in a foreign land." And she bore another, whom he called Eliezer, saying, "For the God of my father, my helper, has rescued me from the hand of Pharaoh."
verses.2:23: Now after much time, the king of Egypt died; and groaning, the sons of Israel cried out because of the labors, and their cry went up to God from the labors.
verses.2:24: And He heard their groaning, and remembered the covenant that He made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.2:25: And the Lord looked upon the sons of Israel and knew them.
verses.3:1: Now Moses was tending the sheep of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian; and when he had driven the flock to the interior of the desert, he came to the mountain of God, Horeb.
verses.3:2: And the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush; and he saw that the bush was burning, and was not being consumed.
verses.3:3: Therefore Moses said, "I will go and see this great sight, why the bush is not consumed."
verses.3:4: Now when the Lord perceived that he was going forward to see, He called him from the midst of the bush and said, "Moses, Moses." And he answered, "I am here."
verses.3:5: But He said, "Do not come near here; untie the footwear from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground."
verses.3:6: And He said, "I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." Moses hid his face, for he did not dare to look toward God.
verses.3:7: The Lord said to him, "I have seen the affliction of My people in Egypt, and I have heard their cry because of the harshness of those who are over the labors;
verses.3:8: and knowing their sorrow, I have come down to deliver them from the hands of the Egyptians, and to bring them out from that land into a good and spacious land, into a land that flows with milk and honey, to the places of the Canaanite and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
verses.3:9: Therefore the cry of the sons of Israel has come to Me, and I have seen their affliction, with which they are oppressed by the Egyptians.
verses.3:10: But come, and I will send you to Pharaoh, so that you may bring out My people, the sons of Israel, from Egypt."
verses.3:11: And Moses said to God, "Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh and bring out the sons of Israel from Egypt?"
verses.3:12: He said to him, "I will be with you; and you will have this as a sign that I have sent you: when you have brought out My people from Egypt, you will sacrifice to God upon this mountain."
verses.3:13: Moses said to God, "Look, I will go to the sons of Israel and say to them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you.' If they say to me, 'What is His name?' what shall I say to them?"
verses.3:14: God said to Moses, "I am who I am." He said, "In this way you shall say to the sons of Israel: 'He Who Is has sent me to you.'"
verses.3:15: And God said again to Moses, "These things you shall say to the sons of Israel: 'The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.' This is My name forever, and this is My memorial from generation to generation.
verses.3:16: Go and gather the elders of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'The Lord God of your fathers has appeared to me, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, saying, "Visiting, I have visited you, and I have seen all the things that have happened to you in Egypt.
verses.3:17: And I have said that I will bring you out from the affliction of Egypt into the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey."'
verses.3:18: And they will listen to your voice; and you and the elders of Israel shall go in to the king of Egypt, and you shall say to him, 'The Lord God of the Hebrews has called us; we will go a journey of three days into the wilderness, so that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God.'
verses.3:19: But I know that the king of Egypt will not release you so that you may go, except by a strong hand.
verses.3:20: For I will stretch out My hand and strike Egypt with all My wonders that I am about to do in the midst of them; after these things he will release you.
verses.3:21: And I will give favor to this people before the Egyptians; and when you go out, you will not depart empty;
verses.3:22: but each woman will ask from her neighbor and from her houseguest for silver and gold vessels and garments; and you will put them upon your sons and your daughters, and you will plunder Egypt."
verses.4:1: Answering, Moses said, "They will not believe me, nor will they listen to my voice, but they will say, 'The Lord has not appeared to you.'"
verses.4:2: Therefore He said to him, "What is it that you are holding in your hand?" He answered, "A staff."
verses.4:3: And the Lord said, "Throw it to the ground." He threw it, and it turned into a snake, so that Moses fled.
verses.4:4: And the Lord said, "Reach out your hand and grasp its tail." He reached out and held it, and it turned into a staff.
verses.4:5: "So that they may believe," He said, "that the Lord God of their fathers has appeared to you, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob."
verses.4:6: And the Lord said again, "Put your hand into your bosom." When he had put it into his bosom, he brought it out leprous, like snow.
verses.4:7: "Draw your hand back," He said, "into your bosom." He drew it back and brought it out again, and it was like the rest of his flesh.
verses.4:8: "If they do not believe you," He said, "nor listen to the message of the first sign, they will believe the word of the following sign.
verses.4:9: And if they do not believe even these two signs, nor listen to your voice, take water from the river and pour it out on the dry ground, and whatever you draw from the river will turn into blood."
verses.4:10: Moses said, "I beg You, Lord, I am not eloquent from yesterday and the day before, and since You have spoken to Your servant, I have a more hindered and slower tongue."
verses.4:11: The Lord said to him, "Who made man's mouth? Or who fashioned the mute and the deaf, the seeing and the blind? Is it not I?
verses.4:12: Go, therefore, and I will be in your mouth, and I will teach you what you are to speak."
verses.4:13: But he said, "I beg You, Lord, send the one whom You are going to send."
verses.4:14: The Lord, angry with Moses, said, "Aaron your brother, the Levite: I know that he is eloquent; look, he himself is coming out to meet you, and seeing you, he will rejoice in his heart.
verses.4:15: Speak to him and put My words in his mouth; and I will be in your mouth and in his mouth, and I will show you what you must do.
verses.4:16: He himself will speak for you to the people, and he will be your mouth; but you will be to him in those things that pertain to God.
verses.4:17: Also take this staff in your hand, with which you are going to perform signs."
verses.4:18: Moses went away and returned to Jethro his father-in-law, and said to him, "I will go and return to my brothers in Egypt, so that I may see if they are still alive." Jethro said to him, "Go in peace."
verses.4:19: Therefore the Lord said to Moses in Midian, "Go and return to Egypt, for all those who were seeking your life are dead."
verses.4:20: Therefore Moses took his wife and his sons and set them on a donkey, and he returned to Egypt, carrying the staff of God in his hand.
verses.4:21: And the Lord said to him as he was returning to Egypt, "See that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders that I have put in your hand; I will harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.
verses.4:22: And you will say to him, 'This is what the Lord says: Israel is My firstborn son.
verses.4:23: I have said to you, "Let My son go so that he may serve Me," and you refused to let him go; look, I will kill your firstborn son.'"
verses.4:24: And when he was on the way, at a lodging place the Lord met him and wanted to kill him.
verses.4:25: Therefore Zipporah took a very sharp stone and circumcised the foreskin of her son, and touched his feet, and said, "You are a bridegroom of blood to me."
verses.4:26: And He let him go after she had said, "A bridegroom of blood because of the circumcision."
verses.4:27: Now the Lord said to Aaron, "Go into the desert to meet Moses." He went to the mountain of God to meet him, and kissed him.
verses.4:28: And Moses told Aaron all the words of the Lord with which He had sent him, and the signs that He had commanded.
verses.4:29: And together they came and gathered all the elders of the sons of Israel.
verses.4:30: And Aaron spoke all the words that the Lord had said to Moses, and he performed the signs before the people,
verses.4:31: and the people believed. And they heard that the Lord had visited the sons of Israel and had looked upon their affliction, and bowing face down, they worshiped.
verses.5:1: After these things Moses and Aaron went in and said to Pharaoh, "This is what the Lord God of Israel says: Let My people go so that they may sacrifice to Me in the desert."
verses.5:2: But he answered, "Who is the Lord, that I should listen to His voice and let Israel go? I do not know the Lord, and I will not let Israel go."
verses.5:3: And they said, "The God of the Hebrews has called us, that we may go a journey of three days into the wilderness and sacrifice to the Lord our God, so that plague or sword may not by chance come upon us."
verses.5:4: The king of Egypt said to them, "Why, Moses and Aaron, do you distract the people from their work? Go to your burdens."
verses.5:5: And Pharaoh said, "The people of the land are numerous; you see that the crowd has increased; how much more if you give them rest from work?"
verses.5:6: Therefore on that day he commanded the overseers of the work and the taskmasters of the people, saying,
verses.5:7: "By no means will you give straw to the people anymore for making bricks, as before; but let them go themselves and gather stubble.
verses.5:8: And you will impose upon them the measure of bricks that they used to make before, nor will you reduce anything; for they are idle, and therefore they cry out, saying, 'Let us go and sacrifice to our God.'
verses.5:9: Let them be weighed down with work, and let them carry it out, so that they may not yield to lying words."
verses.5:10: Therefore the overseers of the work and the taskmasters went out to the people and said, "This is what Pharaoh says: I am not giving you straw;
verses.5:11: go and gather it wherever you can find it, and nothing will be reduced from your work."
verses.5:12: And the people were scattered throughout the whole land of Egypt to gather straw.
verses.5:13: The overseers of the work also pressed hard, saying, "Complete your work daily, just as you used to do before when straw was given to you."
verses.5:14: And those who were over the work of the sons of Israel were flogged by Pharaoh's taskmasters, who said, "Why do you not fulfill the measure of bricks as before, neither yesterday nor today?"
verses.5:15: And the foremen of the sons of Israel came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying, "Why do you act this way against your servants?
verses.5:16: Straw is not given to us, and bricks are demanded just the same; look, we your servants are beaten with whips, and injustice is done against your people."
verses.5:17: He said, "You are idle with leisure, and therefore you say, 'Let us go and sacrifice to the Lord.'
verses.5:18: Go, therefore, and work; straw will not be given to you, and you will deliver the usual number of bricks."
verses.5:19: And the foremen of the sons of Israel saw themselves in trouble, because it was said to them, "Nothing will be reduced from the bricks each day."
verses.5:20: And they met Moses and Aaron, who were standing opposite, as they came out from Pharaoh,
verses.5:21: and they said to them, "May the Lord look and judge, since you have made our odor stink before Pharaoh and his servants, and have offered him a sword so that he might kill us."
verses.5:22: And Moses returned to the Lord and said, "Lord, why have You afflicted this people? Why did You send me?
verses.5:23: For ever since I went in to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, he has afflicted Your people, and You have not delivered them."
verses.6:1: And the Lord said to Moses, "Now you will see what I am about to do to Pharaoh; for by a strong hand he will let them go, and with a mighty hand he will drive them out of his land."
verses.6:2: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "I am the Lord,
verses.6:3: who appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God Almighty, and I did not make My name Adonai known to them.
verses.6:4: And I established a covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojourn, in which they were foreigners.
verses.6:5: I have heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, with which the Egyptians have oppressed them, and I have remembered My covenant.
verses.6:6: Therefore say to the sons of Israel, 'I am the Lord, who will bring you out from the slave prison of the Egyptians, and rescue you from slavery, and redeem you with an uplifted arm and with great judgments.
verses.6:7: And I will take you to Myself as a people, and I will be your God; and you will know that I am the Lord your God, who has brought you out from the slave prison of the Egyptians,
verses.6:8: and has brought you into the land over which I raised My hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and I will give it to you to possess. I am the Lord.'"
verses.6:9: So Moses told everything to the sons of Israel, who did not heed him because of anguish of spirit and the harshest labor.
verses.6:10: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.6:11: "Go in and speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, that he should let the sons of Israel go from his land."
verses.6:12: Moses answered before the Lord, "Look, the sons of Israel do not listen to me; and how will Pharaoh listen, especially since I am uncircumcised in lips?"
verses.6:13: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, and gave a command for the sons of Israel and for Pharaoh, king of Egypt, that they should bring the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
verses.6:14: These are the heads of the houses by their families. The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi;
verses.6:15: these are the clans of Reuben. The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman; these are the descendants of Simeon.
verses.6:16: And these are the names of the sons of Levi by their clans: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Now the years of the life of Levi were one hundred thirty-seven.
verses.6:17: The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, by their clans.
verses.6:18: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath were one hundred thirty-three.
verses.6:19: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of Levi by their families.
verses.6:20: Now Amram took as his wife Jochebed, his paternal cousin, who bore him Aaron and Moses. And the years of the life of Amram were one hundred thirty-seven.
verses.6:21: And the sons of Izhar: Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
verses.6:22: And the sons of Uzziel: Mishael, Elizaphan, and Sithri.
verses.6:23: Now Aaron took as his wife Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, who bore him Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
verses.6:24: And the sons of Korah: Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. These are the clans of the Korahites.
verses.6:25: Moreover, Eleazar, the son of Aaron, took a wife from the daughters of Putiel, who bore him Phinehas. These are the heads of the Levitical families by their clans.
verses.6:26: This is Aaron and Moses, whom the Lord commanded to bring the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their companies.
verses.6:27: These are the ones who speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to bring the sons of Israel out of Egypt; this is Moses and Aaron,
verses.6:28: on the day when the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt.
verses.6:29: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "I am the Lord; speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, everything that I speak to you."
verses.6:30: And Moses said before the Lord, "Look, I am uncircumcised in lips; how will Pharaoh listen to me?"
verses.7:1: And the Lord said to Moses, "Look, I have appointed you as God of Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.
verses.7:2: You will speak to him everything that I command you, and he will speak to Pharaoh, that he should let the sons of Israel go from his land.
verses.7:3: But I will harden his heart, and I will multiply My signs and portents in the land of Egypt,
verses.7:4: and he will not listen to you; and I will lay My hand upon Egypt, and I will bring out My army and My people, the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt by very great judgments.
verses.7:5: And the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord, who has stretched out My hand over Egypt and has brought out the sons of Israel from their midst."
verses.7:6: Therefore Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord had commanded; thus they acted.
verses.7:7: Now Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron was eighty-three, when they spoke to Pharaoh.
verses.7:8: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
verses.7:9: "When Pharaoh says to you, 'Show signs,' you will say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh, and it will be turned into a serpent.'"
verses.7:10: So Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and did just as the Lord had commanded; and Aaron took the staff before Pharaoh and his servants, and it was turned into a serpent.
verses.7:11: Now Pharaoh summoned the wise men and the sorcerers, and they themselves also did likewise through Egyptian incantations and certain secrets.
verses.7:12: And they each threw down their staffs, which were turned into dragons; but Aaron's staff devoured their staffs.
verses.7:13: And Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had commanded.
verses.7:14: Now the Lord said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart is weighed down; he refuses to let the people go.
verses.7:15: Go to him in the morning; look, he will go out to the waters, and you will stand to meet him on the bank of the river, and you will take in your hand the staff that was turned into a dragon.
verses.7:16: And you will say to him, 'The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, "Let My people go, so that they may sacrifice to Me in the wilderness," and up to the present you have refused to listen.
verses.7:17: Therefore this is what the Lord says: "By this you will know that I am the Lord: look, I will strike the water of the river with the staff that is in My hand, and it will be turned into blood.
verses.7:18: The fish also that are in the river will die, and the waters will grow putrid, and the Egyptians will be afflicted drinking the water of the river."'"
verses.7:19: The Lord also said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, and over their rivers, and streams, and marshes, and all pools of water, so that they may be turned into blood; and let there be blood in all the land of Egypt, both in wooden vessels and in stone ones.'"
verses.7:20: And Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord had commanded; and lifting up the staff, he struck the water of the river before Pharaoh and his servants, and it was turned into blood.
verses.7:21: And the fish that were in the river died; and the river grew putrid, and the Egyptians could not drink the water of the river, and there was blood in the whole land of Egypt.
verses.7:22: And the sorcerers of the Egyptians did likewise with their incantations; and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had commanded.
verses.7:23: And he turned away and entered his house, nor did he take it to heart even this time.
verses.7:24: Now all the Egyptians dug all around the river for water to drink, for they could not drink from the water of the river.
verses.7:25: And seven days were completed after the Lord struck the river.
verses.8:1: The Lord also said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh, and you will say to him, 'This is what the Lord says: "Let My people go, so that they may sacrifice to Me;
verses.8:2: but if you refuse to let them go, look, I will strike all your borders with frogs,
verses.8:3: and the river will swarm with frogs, which will come up and enter your house, and the chamber of your bed, and upon your couch, and into the houses of your servants, and among your people, and into your ovens, and into the remains of your food;
verses.8:4: and the frogs will come in to you, and to your people, and to all your servants."'"
verses.8:5: And the Lord said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your hand over the rivers and over the streams and marshes, and bring forth frogs over the land of Egypt.'"
verses.8:6: And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
verses.8:7: But the sorcerers also did likewise through their incantations, and brought forth frogs over the land of Egypt.
verses.8:8: Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said to them, "Pray to the Lord that He may take away the frogs from me and from my people, and I will let the people go so that they may sacrifice to the Lord."
verses.8:9: And Moses said to Pharaoh, "Appoint for me when I should plead for you, and for your servants, and for your people, so that the frogs may be driven away from you, and from your house, and from your servants, and from your people, and remain only in the river."
verses.8:10: He answered, "Tomorrow." And he said, "I will do according to your word, so that you may know that there is no one like the Lord our God.
verses.8:11: And the frogs will depart from you, and from your house, and from your servants, and from your people, and they will remain only in the river."
verses.8:12: And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried out to the Lord regarding the promise about the frogs that he had agreed upon with Pharaoh.
verses.8:13: And the Lord did according to the word of Moses, and the frogs died out of the houses, and out of the farmsteads, and out of the fields.
verses.8:14: And they gathered them into immense heaps, and the land became putrid.
verses.8:15: But Pharaoh, seeing that respite had been given, made his heart heavy and did not listen to them, just as the Lord had commanded.
verses.8:16: And the Lord said to Moses, "Speak to Aaron, 'Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth, and let there be gnats in the entire land of Egypt.'"
verses.8:17: And they did so. And Aaron stretched out his hand, holding the staff, and struck the dust of the earth, and gnats came to be on people and on livestock; all the dust of the earth was turned into gnats throughout the whole land of Egypt.
verses.8:18: And the sorcerers did likewise with their incantations, to bring forth gnats, and they could not; and the gnats were both on people and on livestock.
verses.8:19: And the sorcerers said to Pharaoh, "This is the finger of God." And Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had commanded.
verses.8:20: The Lord also said to Moses, "Rise at daybreak and stand before Pharaoh, for he will go out to the waters; and you will say to him, 'This is what the Lord says: Let My people go so that they may sacrifice to Me.
verses.8:21: But if you do not let them go, look, I will send upon you, and upon your servants, and upon your people, and into your houses, every kind of fly; and the houses of the Egyptians will be filled with flies of various kinds, and the entire land in which they are.
verses.8:22: And on that day I will make marvelous the land of Goshen, in which My people are, so that there will be no flies there, and you may know that I am the Lord in the midst of the earth.
verses.8:23: And I will place a division between My people and your people; tomorrow this sign will take place.'"
verses.8:24: And the Lord did so. And most oppressive flies came into the houses of Pharaoh and of his servants, and into all the land of Egypt; and the land was ruined by flies of this sort.
verses.8:25: And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said to them, "Go and sacrifice to your God in this land."
verses.8:26: And Moses said, "It cannot be done this way; for we will offer in sacrifice the abominations of the Egyptians to the Lord our God. And if we slaughter before them the things that the Egyptians worship, they will overwhelm us with stones.
verses.8:27: We will go a journey of three days into the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to the Lord our God, just as He has commanded us."
verses.8:28: And Pharaoh said, "I will let you go so that you may sacrifice to the Lord your God in the desert; only do not go very far away; pray for me."
verses.8:29: And Moses said, "After going out from you, I will pray to the Lord, and the flies will depart from Pharaoh, and from his servants, and from his people tomorrow; only do not deceive anymore by not letting the people go to sacrifice to the Lord."
verses.8:30: And Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord.
verses.8:31: And He did according to his word, and took away the flies from Pharaoh, and from his servants, and from his people; not even one remained.
verses.8:32: And Pharaoh's heart was made heavy, so that not even this time did he let the people go.
verses.9:1: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and speak to him, 'This is what the Lord God of the Hebrews says: Let My people go so that they may sacrifice to Me.
verses.9:2: But if you still refuse and hold them back,
verses.9:3: look, My hand will be upon your fields, and upon the horses, and donkeys, and camels, and oxen, and sheep, a very severe pestilence.
verses.9:4: And the Lord will do a marvelous thing between the possessions of Israel and the possessions of the Egyptians, so that nothing at all will perish of those things that belong to the sons of Israel.'"
verses.9:5: And the Lord appointed a time, saying, "Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing in the land."
verses.9:6: Therefore the Lord did this thing on the next day, and all the living creatures of the Egyptians died; but of the animals of the sons of Israel, nothing at all perished.
verses.9:7: And Pharaoh sent to see, and nothing was dead of what Israel possessed. And Pharaoh's heart was made heavy, and he did not let the people go.
verses.9:8: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, "Take handfuls of ash from the furnace, and let Moses scatter it toward heaven before Pharaoh.
verses.9:9: And let it be dust over all the land of Egypt; for there will be boils and swelling blisters on people and livestock in the entire land of Egypt."
verses.9:10: And they took ash from the furnace and stood before Pharaoh, and Moses scattered it toward heaven; and boils of swelling blisters formed on people and livestock.
verses.9:11: And the sorcerers could not stand before Moses because of the boils that were on them, and in all the land of Egypt.
verses.9:12: And the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord spoke to Moses.
verses.9:13: And the Lord said to Moses, "Rise in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, and you will say to him, 'This is what the Lord God of the Hebrews says: Let My people go so that they may sacrifice to Me.
verses.9:14: For this time I will send all My plagues upon your heart, and upon your servants, and upon your people, so that you may know that there is no one like Me in all the earth.
verses.9:15: For now, stretching out My hand, I will strike you and your people with pestilence, and you will perish from the earth.
verses.9:16: But for this reason I have appointed you, so that I may show My strength in you, and that My name may be declared in all the earth.
verses.9:17: Do you still hold back My people, and are you unwilling to let them go?
verses.9:18: Look, tomorrow at this very hour I will rain down exceedingly heavy hail, such as has not been in Egypt from the day on which it was founded until the present time.
verses.9:19: Send therefore right now, and gather your livestock and all that you have in the field; for the people, and the livestock, and everything that is found outside and not gathered from the fields, and upon which the hail falls, will die.'"
verses.9:20: Whoever among the servants of Pharaoh feared the word of the Lord made his servants and livestock flee into the houses.
verses.9:21: But whoever neglected the word of the Lord left his servants and livestock in the fields.
verses.9:22: And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that there may be hail in the entire land of Egypt upon people, and upon livestock, and upon every plant of the field in the land of Egypt."
verses.9:23: And Moses stretched out his staff toward heaven, and the Lord sent thunder and hail, and lightning running across the earth; and the Lord rained hail upon the land of Egypt.
verses.9:24: And hail and fire, mingled together, were swept along; and it was of such magnitude as had never before appeared in the entire land of Egypt since that nation was established.
verses.9:25: And the hail struck in all the land of Egypt everything that was in the fields, from human being to livestock; and the hail struck every plant of the field, and shattered every tree of the region.
verses.9:26: Only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel were, did the hail not fall.
verses.9:27: And Pharaoh sent and called Moses and Aaron, saying to them, "I have sinned even now; the Lord is righteous; I and my people are wicked.
verses.9:28: Pray to the Lord that the thunder of God and the hail may cease, so that I may let you go, and you may no longer stay here at all."
verses.9:29: Moses said, "When I have gone out of the city, I will stretch out my palms to the Lord, and the thunder will cease, and there will be no hail, so that you may know that the earth is the Lord's.
verses.9:30: However, I know that both you and your servants do not yet fear the Lord God."
verses.9:31: Therefore the flax and the barley were damaged, because the barley was green, and the flax was already putting forth pods.
verses.9:32: But the wheat and the spelt were not damaged, because they were late-ripening.
verses.9:33: And Moses went out from Pharaoh, out of the city, and stretched out his hands to the Lord; and the thunder and the hail ceased, and rain no longer dripped upon the earth.
verses.9:34: But Pharaoh, seeing that the rain, and the hail, and the thunder had ceased, increased his sin.
verses.9:35: And his heart, and that of his servants, was made heavy and exceedingly hardened; and he did not let the sons of Israel go, just as the Lord had commanded through the hand of Moses.
verses.10:1: And the Lord said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and that of his servants, so that I may perform these signs of Mine in him,
verses.10:2: and that you may recount in the ears of your son and of your grandsons how many times I have crushed the Egyptians and performed My signs among them, and that you may know that I am the Lord."
verses.10:3: So Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and said to him, "This is what the Lord God of the Hebrews says: 'How long do you refuse to be subject to Me? Let My people go, so that they may sacrifice to Me.
verses.10:4: But if you resist and refuse to let them go, look, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your borders,
verses.10:5: which will cover the surface of the land, so that nothing of it may be visible, but what was left over from the hail will be eaten; for they will eat away all the trees that sprout in the fields.
verses.10:6: And they will fill your houses, and those of your servants, and of all the Egyptians, such as your fathers and grandfathers have not seen since the time they came into being upon the earth until the present day.'" And he turned away and went out from Pharaoh.
verses.10:7: Then Pharaoh's servants said to him, "How long will we endure this stumbling block? Let the men go, so that they may sacrifice to the Lord their God; do you not see that Egypt has perished?"
verses.10:8: And they called Moses and Aaron back to Pharaoh, who said to them, "Go, sacrifice to the Lord your God; who exactly are the ones who will go?"
verses.10:9: Moses said, "With our little ones and elders we will go, with our sons and daughters, with our sheep and herds; for it is a solemn feast of the Lord our God."
verses.10:10: And Pharaoh answered, "So may the Lord be with you, just as I will let you and your little ones go! Who doubts that you are plotting most wickedly?
verses.10:11: It will not be so; instead, go, you men only, and sacrifice to the Lord, for this is what you yourselves asked for." And immediately they were driven out from Pharaoh's presence.
verses.10:12: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, so that they may come up over it and devour all the vegetation that was left over from the hail."
verses.10:13: And Moses stretched out the staff over the land of Egypt, and the Lord brought in a scorching wind all that day and night; and when morning came, the scorching wind lifted up the locusts.
verses.10:14: And they came up over the entire land of Egypt and settled, innumerable, within all the borders of the Egyptians, such as had not been before that time, nor will be afterward.
verses.10:15: And they covered the entire surface of the land, devastating everything. Therefore the vegetation of the land was devoured, and whatever fruit was on the trees that the hail had left behind; and nothing green at all was left on the trees or on the plants of the land, in all Egypt.
verses.10:16: For this reason Pharaoh hurriedly called Moses and Aaron and said to them, "I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
verses.10:17: But now forgive me my sin even this once, and plead with the Lord your God that He may take away this death from me."
verses.10:18: And Moses went out from Pharaoh's presence and prayed to the Lord.
verses.10:19: And He caused a very strong wind to blow from the west, and seizing the locusts, He cast them into the Red Sea; not even a single one remained within all the borders of Egypt.
verses.10:20: And the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the sons of Israel go.
verses.10:21: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the sky, and let there be darkness over the land of Egypt, so dense that it can be felt."
verses.10:22: And Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and there was dreadful darkness in the entire land of Egypt for three days.
verses.10:23: No one saw his brother, nor moved from the place where he was; but wherever the sons of Israel lived, there was light.
verses.10:24: And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said to them, "Go, sacrifice to the Lord. Only let your sheep and herds remain behind; your little ones may go with you."
verses.10:25: Moses said, "You will also give us sacrifices and burnt offerings that we may offer to the Lord our God.
verses.10:26: All the flocks will go with us; not a hoof of them will remain behind, for they are necessary for the worship of the Lord our God, especially since we do not know what must be offered in sacrifice until we reach the place itself."
verses.10:27: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
verses.10:28: And Pharaoh said to Moses, "Go away from me, and be careful not to see my face again; on whatever day you appear before me, you will die."
verses.10:29: Moses answered, "So it will be, as you have spoken; I will not see your face again."
verses.11:1: And the Lord said to Moses, "With one more plague I will strike Pharaoh and Egypt, and after this he will let you go and compel you to go out.
verses.11:2: Therefore tell all the people that each man is to ask his friend, and each woman her neighbor, for silver and gold vessels.
verses.11:3: And the Lord will give favor to His people in the sight of the Egyptians." And Moses was a very great man in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh's servants and all the people.
verses.11:4: And he said, "This is what the Lord says: 'At midnight I will go out into Egypt,
verses.11:5: and every firstborn in the land of the Egyptians will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sits on his throne, to the firstborn of the female servant who is at the mill, and all the firstborn of the livestock.
verses.11:6: And there will be a great outcry in the entire land of Egypt, such as has neither been before nor will be afterward.
verses.11:7: But among all the sons of Israel not a dog will make a sound, from man to beast, so that you may know by what a great miracle the Lord separates the Egyptians and Israel.'
verses.11:8: And all these servants of yours will come down to me and bow down to me, saying, 'Go out, you and all the people who are subject to you.' After this we will go out."
verses.11:9: And he went out from Pharaoh very angry. Then the Lord said to Moses, "Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that many signs may be done in the land of Egypt."
verses.11:10: Now Moses and Aaron performed before Pharaoh all the wonders that are written. And the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the sons of Israel go from his land.
verses.12:1: The Lord also said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt:
verses.12:2: "This month shall be for you the beginning of months; it shall be the first among the months of the year.
verses.12:3: Speak to the entire assembly of the sons of Israel and say to them, 'On the tenth day of this month, let each one take a lamb according to their families and houses.
verses.12:4: But if the number is too small to suffice for eating the lamb, he shall take his neighbor who is next to his house, according to the number of souls that can suffice for the eating of the lamb.
verses.12:5: Now the lamb shall be without blemish, a male, one year old; according to this same rite you shall also take a young goat.
verses.12:6: And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month, and the entire multitude of the sons of Israel shall sacrifice it at evening.
verses.12:7: And they shall take some of its blood and put it on both doorposts and on the lintels of the houses in which they will eat it.
verses.12:8: And they shall eat the meat that night, roasted with fire, and unleavened loaves with wild lettuce.
verses.12:9: You shall not eat anything of it raw, nor boiled in water, but only roasted with fire; you shall consume the head along with its feet and entrails.
verses.12:10: Nor shall anything of it remain until morning; if anything is left over, you shall burn it up with fire.
verses.12:11: Now you shall eat it in this way: you shall gird your waist, and have sandals on your feet, holding staffs in your hands, and you shall eat hurriedly; for it is the Passover (that is, the passing over) of the Lord.
verses.12:12: And I will pass through the land of Egypt on that night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments. I am the Lord.
verses.12:13: Now the blood will be a sign for you on the houses in which you will be; and I will see the blood, and I will pass over you, nor will there be a destroying plague among you when I strike the land of Egypt.
verses.12:14: Now you shall hold this day as a memorial, and you shall celebrate it as a solemn festival to the Lord throughout your generations with everlasting worship.
verses.12:15: For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; on the first day there shall be no leaven in your houses. Whoever eats anything leavened, that soul shall perish from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day.
verses.12:16: The first day shall be holy and solemn, and the seventh day revered with the same festivity; you shall do no work on them, except for those things that pertain to eating.
verses.12:17: And you shall observe the unleavened bread; for on this very same day I will bring your army out of the land of Egypt, and you shall keep this day throughout your generations by a perpetual rite.
verses.12:18: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, you shall eat unleavened bread until the twenty-first day of the same month at evening.
verses.12:19: For seven days leaven shall not be found in your houses. Whoever eats anything leavened, his soul shall perish from the assembly of Israel, whether from the strangers or from the natives of the land.
verses.12:20: You shall not eat anything leavened; in all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.'"
verses.12:21: Then Moses called all the elders of the sons of Israel and said to them, "Go, taking an animal according to your families, and sacrifice the Passover.
verses.12:22: And dip a bundle of hyssop in the blood that is on the threshold, and sprinkle the lintel and both doorposts with it; let none of you go out of the doorway of his house until morning.
verses.12:23: For the Lord will pass through, striking the Egyptians; and when He sees the blood on the lintel and on both doorposts, He will pass over the doorway of the house, and He will not permit the striker to enter your houses and do harm.
verses.12:24: Keep this word as a statute for you and your sons forever.
verses.12:25: And when you enter the land that the Lord is going to give you, as He promised, you shall observe these ceremonies.
verses.12:26: And when your sons say to you, 'What is this religious observance?'
verses.12:27: you shall say to them, 'It is the sacrifice of the passing over of the Lord, when He passed over the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt, striking the Egyptians and delivering our houses.'" And the people bowed down and worshiped.
verses.12:28: And the sons of Israel went out and did just as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.
verses.12:29: Now it happened in the middle of the night that the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive woman who was in prison, and every firstborn of the livestock.
verses.12:30: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, and all his servants, and all Egypt; and a great outcry arose in Egypt, for there was no house in which a dead person did not lie.
verses.12:31: And having called Moses and Aaron in the night, Pharaoh said, "Rise and go out from my people, you and the sons of Israel; go, sacrifice to the Lord as you say.
verses.12:32: Take your sheep and your herds as you had asked, and as you depart, bless me."
verses.12:33: And the Egyptians urged the people to go out of the land quickly, saying, "We will all die."
verses.12:34: Therefore the people took the kneaded flour before it was leavened, and tying it up in cloaks, they placed it on their shoulders.
verses.12:35: And the sons of Israel did just as Moses had commanded, and they asked of the Egyptians silver and gold vessels and very much clothing.
verses.12:36: Now the Lord gave favor to the people before the Egyptians, so that they lent to them; and they plundered the Egyptians.
verses.12:37: And the sons of Israel set out from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides the little ones.
verses.12:38: And a countless mixed crowd also went up with them, sheep and herds and animals of various kinds, exceedingly many.
verses.12:39: And they baked the flour that they had previously brought kneaded out of Egypt, and they made unleavened loaves baked under the ashes; for they could not be leavened, as the Egyptians were forcing them to leave and allowing them to make no delay, nor had there been opportunity to prepare any provisions.
verses.12:40: Now the dwelling of the sons of Israel, during which they remained in Egypt, was four hundred thirty years.
verses.12:41: When these were completed, on that same day the entire army of the Lord went out of the land of Egypt.
verses.12:42: This night is to be observed for the Lord, when He brought them out of the land of Egypt; all the sons of Israel must observe this night throughout their generations.
verses.12:43: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, "This is the religious observance of the Passover: no foreigner shall eat of it.
verses.12:44: But every purchased servant shall be circumcised, and thus he shall eat.
verses.12:45: A stranger and a hired worker shall not eat of it.
verses.12:46: It shall be eaten in one house; you shall not carry any of its meat outside, nor shall you break a bone of it.
verses.12:47: The entire assembly of the sons of Israel shall keep it.
verses.12:48: And if any of the sojourners wishes to cross over into your settlement and keep the Passover of the Lord, every male belonging to him shall first be circumcised, and then he shall celebrate it according to the rite, and he shall be like a native of the land. But if anyone has not been circumcised, he shall not eat of it.
verses.12:49: The same law shall be for the native and for the settler who sojourns among you."
verses.12:50: And all the sons of Israel did just as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.
verses.12:51: And on that same day the Lord brought the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their companies.
verses.13:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.13:2: "Sanctify to Me every firstborn that opens the womb among the sons of Israel, both of humans and of beasts, for all are Mine."
verses.13:3: And Moses said to the people, "Remember this day on which you went out from Egypt and from the house of slavery, because with a strong hand the Lord brought you out from this place, so that you may not eat leavened bread.
verses.13:4: Today you are going out, in the month of new crops.
verses.13:5: And when the Lord has brought you into the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, which He swore to your fathers that He would give to you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you will celebrate this custom of sacred rites in this month.
verses.13:6: For seven days you will eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there will be a solemn feast of the Lord.
verses.13:7: You will eat unleavened bread for seven days; nothing leavened will appear with you, nor in all your borders.
verses.13:8: And you will tell your son on that day, saying, 'This is what the Lord did for me when I went out from Egypt.'
verses.13:9: And it will be like a sign on your hand, and like a memorial before your eyes, and so that the law of the Lord may always be in your mouth, for with a strong hand the Lord brought you out from Egypt.
verses.13:10: You will keep this kind of observance at the appointed time, from days to days.
verses.13:11: And when the Lord has brought you into the land of the Canaanite, just as He swore to you and to your fathers, and has given it to you,
verses.13:12: you will set apart everything that opens the womb to the Lord, and what is firstborn among your livestock; whatever you have of the male sex, you will consecrate to the Lord.
verses.13:13: You will exchange the firstborn of a donkey for a sheep, and if you do not redeem it, you will kill it. Yet every firstborn of man among your sons you will redeem with a price.
verses.13:14: And when your son asks you tomorrow, saying, 'What is this?' you will answer him, 'With a strong hand the Lord brought us out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.
verses.13:15: For when Pharaoh had become hardened and was unwilling to let us go, the Lord killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of man up to the firstborn of beasts; for that reason I sacrifice to the Lord everything that opens the womb of the male sex, and I redeem all the firstborn of my sons.'
verses.13:16: Therefore it will be like a sign on your hand, and like something hung, for remembrance, between your eyes, because with a strong hand the Lord brought us out from Egypt."
verses.13:17: Therefore, when Pharaoh had sent the people out, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, which is nearby, thinking that perhaps they might regret it if they saw wars rising up against them, and return to Egypt.
verses.13:18: But He led them around by the way of the desert, which is beside the Red Sea; and the sons of Israel went up armed from the land of Egypt.
verses.13:19: Moses also took the bones of Joseph with him, because he had bound the sons of Israel by an oath, saying, "God will visit you; carry my bones out from here with you."
verses.13:20: And setting out from Succoth, they encamped in Etham, at the farthest borders of the wilderness.
verses.13:21: Now the Lord was going ahead of them to show the way, by day in a pillar of cloud and by night in a pillar of fire, so that He might be the guide of the journey at both times.
verses.13:22: Never was the pillar of cloud absent by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, before the people.
verses.14:1: Now the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.14:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel: let them turn back and encamp facing Pi-hahiroth, which is between Migdol and the sea, opposite Baal-zephon; in sight of it you will pitch camp by the sea.
verses.14:3: And Pharaoh will say concerning the sons of Israel, 'They are hemmed in within the land; the desert has shut them in.'
verses.14:4: And I will harden his heart, and he will pursue you; and I will be glorified in Pharaoh and in all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord." And they did so.
verses.14:5: And it was reported to the king of the Egyptians that the people had fled; and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was changed regarding the people, and they said, "What did we mean to do, that we let Israel go so that they would not serve us?"
verses.14:6: Therefore he harnessed the chariot, and took all his people with him.
verses.14:7: And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and whatever chariots were in Egypt, and the commanders of the whole army.
verses.14:8: And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued the sons of Israel; yet they went out with an uplifted hand.
verses.14:9: And as the Egyptians were pursuing the tracks of those going ahead, they found them in camp by the sea; all the cavalry and chariots of Pharaoh, and the entire army, were at Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon.
verses.14:10: And when Pharaoh had drawn near, the sons of Israel, lifting up their eyes, saw the Egyptians behind them, and they feared greatly, and cried out to the Lord,
verses.14:11: and said to Moses, "Perhaps there were no graves in Egypt; therefore you took us so that we would die in the wilderness. Why did you want to do this, to bring us out of Egypt?
verses.14:12: Is this not the word that we were speaking to you in Egypt, saying, 'Withdraw from us, so that we may serve the Egyptians'? For it was much better to serve them than to die in the wilderness."
verses.14:13: And Moses said to the people, "Do not fear; stand, and see the great works of the Lord that He is about to do today; for the Egyptians whom you see now, you will by no means see again, forever.
verses.14:14: The Lord will fight for you, and you will be silent."
verses.14:15: And the Lord said to Moses, "Why are you crying out to Me? Speak to the sons of Israel so that they may set out.
verses.14:16: And you, lift up your staff, and stretch out your hand over the sea, and divide it, so that the sons of Israel may walk in the middle of the sea across dry ground.
verses.14:17: And I will harden the heart of the Egyptians, so that they may pursue you; and I will be glorified in Pharaoh, and in all his army, and in his chariots and in his horsemen.
verses.14:18: And the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord, when I have been glorified in Pharaoh, and in his chariots and in his horsemen."
verses.14:19: And the angel of God, who was going ahead of the camp of Israel, lifted himself up and went behind them; and together with him the pillar of cloud, leaving the front, in the rear
verses.14:20: stood between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and the cloud was dark, and lighting up the night, so that they were unable to approach one another throughout the whole time of the night.
verses.14:21: And when Moses had stretched out his hand over the sea, the Lord removed it with a strong and burning wind blowing all night, and turned it into dry ground; and the water was divided.
verses.14:22: And the sons of Israel went in through the middle of the dry sea, for the water was like a wall on their right and on their left.
verses.14:23: And the Egyptians, pursuing, went in after them, and all the cavalry of Pharaoh, his chariots and horsemen, through the middle of the sea.
verses.14:24: And already the morning watch had arrived, and look, the Lord, looking down upon the camp of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of cloud, killed their army,
verses.14:25: and overturned the wheels of the chariots, and they were carried into the deep. Therefore the Egyptians said, "Let us flee from Israel, for the Lord is fighting for them against us."
verses.14:26: And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea, so that the waters may return to the Egyptians, over their chariots and horsemen."
verses.14:27: And when Moses had stretched out his hand toward the sea, it returned at first dawn to its former place; and the waters met the fleeing Egyptians, and the Lord enveloped them in the middle of the waves.
verses.14:28: And the waters returned and covered the chariots and horsemen of all the army of Pharaoh, who, following, had gone into the sea; not even one of them survived.
verses.14:29: But the sons of Israel proceeded through the middle of the dry sea, and the waters were to them as if a wall on the right and on the left;
verses.14:30: and the Lord delivered Israel on that day from the hand of the Egyptians.
verses.14:31: And they saw the Egyptians dead on the shore of the sea, and the great hand that the Lord had exercised against them; and the people feared the Lord, and they believed the Lord, and Moses His servant.
verses.15:1: Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to the Lord, and they said, "Let us sing to the Lord, for He has been magnified gloriously; He has hurled down the horse and the rider into the sea.
verses.15:2: My strength and my praise is the Lord, and He has become salvation for me; this is my God, and I will glorify Him; the God of my father, and I will exalt Him.
verses.15:3: The Lord is like a fighting man; Almighty is His name.
verses.15:4: Pharaoh's chariots and his army He flung into the sea; his chosen leaders were submerged in the Red Sea.
verses.15:5: The depths covered them; they went down into the deep like a stone.
verses.15:6: Your right hand, Lord, has been magnified in strength; Your right hand, Lord, struck the enemy.
verses.15:7: And in the abundance of Your glory You brought down Your adversaries; You sent Your wrath, which devoured them like stubble.
verses.15:8: And by the breath of Your fury the waters were gathered together; the flowing wave stood still; the depths were gathered together in the middle of the sea.
verses.15:9: The enemy said, 'I will pursue and overtake, I will divide the spoils, my soul will be filled; I will unsheathe my sword, my hand will kill them.'
verses.15:10: Your breath blew, and the sea covered them; they were submerged like lead in the violent waters.
verses.15:11: Who is like You among the mighty, Lord? Who is like You, magnificent in holiness, fearsome and praiseworthy, doing wonders?
verses.15:12: You stretched out Your hand, and the earth devoured them.
verses.15:13: You have been a guide in Your mercy to the people whom You redeemed, and You carried them in Your strength to Your holy dwelling.
verses.15:14: The peoples went up and became angry; pangs took hold of the inhabitants of Philistia.
verses.15:15: Then the leaders of Edom were thrown into turmoil; trembling took hold of the strong men of Moab; all the inhabitants of Canaan grew rigid.
verses.15:16: May dread and terror rush upon them in the greatness of Your arm; may they become motionless like a stone, until Your people pass through, Lord, until this people of Yours, whom You have possessed, pass through.
verses.15:17: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance, Your most firm dwelling that You have made, Lord; Your sanctuary, Lord, which Your hands have made firm.
verses.15:18: The Lord will reign forever and beyond."
verses.15:19: For Pharaoh entered the sea on horseback with his chariots and his horsemen, and the Lord brought the waters of the sea back over them; the sons of Israel, however, walked across dry ground in the middle of it.
verses.15:20: So Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and dances,
verses.15:21: and before them she led the song, saying, "Let us sing to the Lord, for He has been magnified gloriously; He has hurled down the horse and its rider into the sea."
verses.15:22: Now Moses led Israel away from the Red Sea, and they went out into the desert of Shur; and they walked for three days through the wilderness, and they did not find water.
verses.15:23: And they came to Marah, and they could not drink the waters from Marah because they were bitter; therefore he also assigned a fitting name to the place, calling it Marah, that is, bitterness.
verses.15:24: And the people grumbled against Moses, saying, "What will we drink?"
verses.15:25: But he cried out to the Lord, who showed him a piece of wood; and when he had cast it into the waters, they were turned into sweetness. There He established precepts and judgments for him, and there He tested him,
verses.15:26: saying, "If you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and do what is right before Him, and obey His commandments, and keep all His precepts, none of the sickness that I put in Egypt will I bring upon you; for I am the Lord, your healer."
verses.15:27: Then the sons of Israel came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees; and they camped beside the waters.
verses.16:1: And they set out from Elim, and the whole multitude of the sons of Israel came into the desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had gone out from the land of Egypt.
verses.16:2: And the whole congregation of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.
verses.16:3: And the sons of Israel said to them, "If only we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat over the pots of meat and ate bread to the full! Why have you brought us out into this desert, to kill the whole multitude with hunger?"
verses.16:4: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Look, I will rain bread for you from heaven; let the people go out and gather what is enough for each day, so that I may test them, whether they walk in My law or not.
verses.16:5: And on the sixth day let them prepare what they bring in, and let it be double what they were accustomed to gather each day."
verses.16:6: And Moses and Aaron said to all the sons of Israel, "In the evening you will know that the Lord brought you out from the land of Egypt,
verses.16:7: and in the morning you will see the glory of the Lord, for He has heard your grumbling against the Lord. Indeed, what are we, that you have muttered against us?"
verses.16:8: And Moses said, "The Lord will give you meat to eat in the evening, and bread to the full in the morning, because He has heard your grumblings with which you have grumbled against Him. For what are we? Your grumbling is not against us, but against the Lord."
verses.16:9: Moses also said to Aaron, "Say to the entire congregation of the sons of Israel, 'Come near before the Lord, for He has heard your grumbling.'"
verses.16:10: And while Aaron was speaking to the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, they looked toward the wilderness, and look, the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud.
verses.16:11: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.16:12: "I have heard the grumblings of the sons of Israel. Speak to them: 'In the evening you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread, and you will know that I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.16:13: So it came about in the evening that quail came up and covered the camp; in the morning also, dew lay all around the camp.
verses.16:14: And when it had covered the surface of the earth, there appeared in the wilderness something fine, and as if pounded with a pestle, in the likeness of frost upon the earth.
verses.16:15: And when the sons of Israel saw it, they said to one another, "Manhu?" which means, "What is this?" for they did not know what it was. To them Moses said, "This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
verses.16:16: This is the word that the Lord has commanded: 'Let each one gather from it as much as is enough to eat: an omer per head, according to the number of your souls who live in the tent; so you will take it.'"
verses.16:17: And the sons of Israel did so; and they gathered, some more, some less.
verses.16:18: And they measured by the measure of an omer; and the one who had gathered more had nothing extra, nor did the one who had prepared less find less; rather, they each collected according to what they were able to eat.
verses.16:19: And Moses said to them, "Let no one leave any of it until morning."
verses.16:20: Yet they did not listen to him, but some of them left it until morning, and it began to swarm with worms and rotted; and Moses was angry with them.
verses.16:21: Now they gathered in the morning, each one as much as could be enough to eat; and when the sun had grown hot, it melted.
verses.16:22: On the sixth day, however, they gathered double food, that is, two omers for each person; and all the leaders of the multitude came and reported to Moses.
verses.16:23: He said to them, "This is what the Lord has spoken: 'The rest of the Sabbath is sanctified to the Lord tomorrow; whatever is to be made, do it, and what is to be cooked, cook; whatever is left over, however, set aside until morning.'"
verses.16:24: And they did just as Moses had commanded, and it did not rot, nor was a worm found in it.
verses.16:25: And Moses said, "Eat it today, because it is the Sabbath of the Lord; today it will not be found in the field.
verses.16:26: For six days gather it; on the seventh day, however, is the Sabbath of the Lord; therefore it will not be found."
verses.16:27: And the seventh day came; and some of the people went out to gather, and they did not find any.
verses.16:28: Then the Lord said to Moses, "How long do you refuse to keep My commandments and My law?
verses.16:29: See that the Lord has given you the Sabbath, and because of this on the sixth day He gives you double food; let each one remain where he is; let no one go out from his place on the seventh day."
verses.16:30: And the people kept the Sabbath on the seventh day.
verses.16:31: And the house of Israel called its name Manna; it was white like coriander seed, and its taste was like fine flour with honey.
verses.16:32: Then Moses said, "This is the word that the Lord has commanded: 'Fill an omer from it, and let it be kept for future generations to come, so that they may know the bread with which I nourished you in the wilderness, when you were brought out from the land of Egypt.'"
verses.16:33: And Moses said to Aaron, "Take one vessel, and put manna in it, as much as an omer can hold, and place it before the Lord to be preserved for your generations,"
verses.16:34: just as the Lord commanded Moses. And Aaron placed it in the tabernacle to be preserved.
verses.16:35: Now the sons of Israel ate manna for forty years, until they came to a habitable land; with this food they were nourished until they touched the borders of the land of Canaan.
verses.16:36: Now an omer is the tenth part of an ephah.
verses.17:1: Therefore the entire multitude of the sons of Israel, having set out from the desert of Sin by their stages according to the word of the Lord, encamped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.17:2: And they disputed with Moses and said, "Give us water, so that we may drink." To them Moses replied, "Why do you dispute with me? Why do you test the Lord?"
verses.17:3: So the people thirsted there because of the lack of water, and grumbled against Moses, saying, "Why did you make us come out of Egypt to kill us, our children, and livestock with thirst?"
verses.17:4: Then Moses cried out to the Lord, saying, "What should I do with this people? A little longer, and they will stone me."
verses.17:5: And the Lord said to Moses, "Go ahead of the people, and take with you some of the elders of Israel; and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the river, and go.
verses.17:6: Look, I will stand there before you on the rock of Horeb; and you will strike the rock, and water will come out of it, so that the people may drink." Moses did so before the elders of Israel,
verses.17:7: and he called the name of that place Testing, because of the dispute of the sons of Israel, and because they tested the Lord, saying, "Is the Lord among us, or not?"
verses.17:8: Then Amalek came and fought against Israel at Rephidim.
verses.17:9: And Moses said to Joshua, "Choose men, and go out and fight against Amalek; tomorrow I will stand on the summit of the hill, holding the staff of God in my hand."
verses.17:10: Joshua did as Moses had spoken and fought against Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the summit of the hill.
verses.17:11: And whenever Moses raised his hands, Israel was winning; but if he lowered them a little, Amalek prevailed.
verses.17:12: But the hands of Moses were heavy; therefore, taking a stone, they placed it beneath him, on which he sat, and Aaron and Hur supported his hands on either side. And it came about that his hands did not grow weary until the setting of the sun.
verses.17:13: And Joshua put Amalek and his people to flight with the edge of the sword.
verses.17:14: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Write this as a memorial in a book, and deliver it to the ears of Joshua; for I will blot out the memory of Amalek under heaven."
verses.17:15: And Moses built an altar and called its name "The Lord Is My Exaltation," saying,
verses.17:16: "Because the hand of the throne of the Lord, and the war of the Lord, will be against Amalek from generation to generation."
verses.18:1: And when Jethro, priest of Midian, the relative of Moses, had heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel His people, and that the Lord had brought Israel out of Egypt,
verses.18:2: he took Zipporah, the wife of Moses, whom he had sent back,
verses.18:3: and her two sons, one of whom was called Gershom, his father saying, "I have been a sojourner in a foreign land";
verses.18:4: and the other Eliezer: "For the God of my father," he said, "is my helper, and He rescued me from the sword of Pharaoh."
verses.18:5: Therefore Jethro, the relative of Moses, and his sons and his wife came to Moses in the desert, where he had encamped beside the mountain of God.
verses.18:6: And he sent word to Moses, saying, "I, Jethro your relative, am coming to you, and your wife, and the two sons with her."
verses.18:7: And he went out to meet his relative, bowed down, and kissed him; and they greeted one another with words of peace. And when he had entered the tent,
verses.18:8: Moses recounted to his relative everything that the Lord had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians on account of Israel, and all the hardship that had happened to them on the journey, and that the Lord had delivered them.
verses.18:9: And Jethro rejoiced over all the good things that the Lord had done for Israel, because He had rescued them from the hand of the Egyptians.
verses.18:10: And he said, "Blessed be the Lord, who delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of Pharaoh, who rescued His people from the hand of Egypt.
verses.18:11: Now I know that the Lord is great above all gods, because they acted arrogantly against them."
verses.18:12: Therefore Jethro, the relative of Moses, offered burnt offerings and sacrifices to God; and Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with him before God.
verses.18:13: Now on the next day Moses sat to judge the people, who stood before Moses from morning until evening.
verses.18:14: And when his relative saw this, namely everything that he was doing among the people, he said, "What is this that you are doing among the people? Why do you sit alone, and all the people wait from morning until evening?"
verses.18:15: Moses replied to him, "The people come to me seeking the judgment of God;
verses.18:16: and whenever any dispute arises among them, they come to me so that I may judge between them and show the precepts of God and His laws."
verses.18:17: But he said, "You are not doing a good thing.
verses.18:18: You will be worn out with foolish labor, both you and this people who are with you; the task is beyond your strength; you will not be able to bear it alone.
verses.18:19: But listen to my words and counsels, and God will be with you. Be for the people in the things that pertain to God, so that you may report to Him what is said,
verses.18:20: and show the people the ceremonies and the rite of worship, and the way in which they ought to walk, and the work that they ought to do.
verses.18:21: Moreover, select from all the people capable men who fear God, in whom there is truth, and who hate greed, and appoint from them tribunes, centurions, leaders of fifty, and leaders of ten,
verses.18:22: to judge the people at all times; and whatever is greater, let them bring to you, while they themselves judge only the smaller matters, so that it may be lighter for you, with the burden divided among others.
verses.18:23: If you do this, you will fulfill the command of God, and you will be able to uphold His precepts, and all this people will return to their own places in peace."
verses.18:24: Having heard these things, Moses did everything that he had suggested.
verses.18:25: And having chosen vigorous men from all Israel, he appointed them rulers of the people: tribunes, centurions, leaders of fifty, and leaders of ten.
verses.18:26: And they judged the people at all times; whatever was more serious they brought to him, judging only the easier matters.
verses.18:27: And he let his relative go, who returned and departed to his own land.
verses.19:1: In the third month of the departure of Israel from the land of Egypt, on this day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.
verses.19:2: For having set out from Rephidim and arriving as far as the desert of Sinai, they encamped in that same place, and there Israel pitched tents opposite the mountain.
verses.19:3: Now Moses went up to God; and the Lord called to him from the mountain and said, "These things you will say to the house of Jacob, and announce to the sons of Israel:
verses.19:4: 'You yourselves have seen what I did to the Egyptians, how I carried you on the wings of eagles and took you to Myself.
verses.19:5: If therefore you listen to My voice and keep My covenant, you will be to Me a special possession out of all peoples, for all the earth is Mine;
verses.19:6: and you will be to Me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation.' These are the words that you will speak to the sons of Israel."
verses.19:7: Moses came, and having summoned the elders of the people, he set forth all the words that the Lord had commanded.
verses.19:8: And all the people answered together, "Everything that the Lord has spoken, we will do." And when Moses had reported the words of the people to the Lord,
verses.19:9: the Lord said to him, "Even now I will come to you in the darkness of a cloud, so that the people may hear Me speaking to you and believe you forever." Therefore Moses declared the words of the people to the Lord.
verses.19:10: And He said to him, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments.
verses.19:11: And let them be ready for the third day; for on the third day the Lord will come down before all the people upon Mount Sinai.
verses.19:12: And you will set boundaries for the people all around, and you will say to them, 'Be careful that you do not go up onto the mountain, nor touch its borders.' Everyone who touches the mountain will surely die.
verses.19:13: No hand will touch him, but he will be crushed with stones or pierced with javelins; whether it is a beast or a human, it will not live; when the trumpet begins to sound, then let them go up onto the mountain."
verses.19:14: And Moses came down from the mountain to the people and consecrated them. And when they had washed their garments,
verses.19:15: he said to them, "Be ready for the third day, and do not draw near to your wives."
verses.19:16: And now the third day had arrived, and morning had brightened; and look, thunder began to be heard, and lightning to flash, and a very dense cloud to cover the mountain, and the blast of the trumpet rang out very loudly; and the people who were in the camp were afraid.
verses.19:17: And when Moses had brought them out from the place of the camp to meet God, they stood at the foot of the mountain.
verses.19:18: Now all of Mount Sinai was smoking, because the Lord had come down upon it in fire, and smoke rose from it as from a furnace; and the entire mountain was terrifying.
verses.19:19: And the sound of the trumpet gradually grew louder and was drawn out longer; Moses spoke, and God answered him.
verses.19:20: And the Lord came down upon Mount Sinai, on the very summit of the mountain, and called Moses to its peak. And when he had gone up there,
